primary.title: IPO Calendar: Primary market cools after Jio frenzy, but 13 listings lined up
primary.description: India's primary market is set for a quiet week after a series of large public offerings, with just one new IPO worth Rs 57 crore scheduled to open for subscription between November 2 and November 6. There will be no fresh mainboard IPO launches, although several companies that raised funds in late October are preparing for their stock market debuts.Vedant Poly Fabs, a small and medium enterprise (SME), will be the only new company opening its IPO next week. Meanwhile, six companies whose public issues are currently open, including mainboard player Bombay Coated & Special Steels, are scheduled to list on the exchanges during the week.The slowdown follows a busy October for India's primary market, highlighted by Jio Platforms' Rs 30,188 crore IPO, the largest in the country's history.Mukesh Ambani-led Jio made its stock market debut on October 28 at Rs 1,358, a premium of 21.36% over its issue price of Rs 1,119. The blockbuster offering attracted bids worth Rs 4.9 lakh crore in the public book and was subscribed more than 22 times.The coming week will see investors turn their attention towards the final subscription days of existing issues and the listing performance of recently concluded offerings.Vedant Poly Fabs IPOThe Rs 56.68 crore IPO of Vedant Poly Fabs will open for public subscription on Monday, November 2, and close on Wednesday, November 4. The company has fixed a price band of Rs 88-94 per share.The offering comprises a fresh issue of 54.26 lakh shares worth Rs 51.01 crore and an offer for sale of 6.04 lakh shares aggregating to Rs 5.67 crore. Retail investors will have to apply for a minimum of 2,400 shares, requiring an investment of Rs 2,25,600 at the upper end of the price band.The company is expected to finalise the basis of allotment on November 5, with its tentative listing on the NSE SME platform scheduled for November 9.Vedant Poly Fabs manufactures flexible packaging materials, including shrink films, printed laminates and packaging pouches used in the food, beverage and consumer goods industries.13 ongoing IPOs headed for listingAmong the existing issues continuing into next week, Bombay Coated & Special Steels will be the mainboard offering in focus. The company's Rs 183.06 crore IPO, which opened on October 29, will close for subscription on November 2.The price band has been fixed at Rs 78-82 per share, with a minimum retail application of 182 shares, requiring an investment of Rs 14,924. The IPO is entirely a fresh issue of 2.23 crore equity shares.The company plans to utilise Rs 125 crore towards repayment of borrowings and Rs 15.77 crore to acquire capital equipment under existing lease arrangements.Bombay Coated operates in steel processing, converting coils into products used by automotive, appliance and engineering manufacturers. The issue received a strong response during its first two days of bidding, with subscription reaching 3.98 times on October 30. The qualified institutional buyer portion was subscribed 6.89 times, while the retail category attracted 3.17 times bids.The allotment is expected to be finalised on November 3, with shares scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on November 5. Bombay Coated is the only mainboard company among these six that will list this week.The wider IPO calendar also includes listings of companies whose subscription periods ended last week. EAAA India Alternatives is scheduled to debut on November 2, followed by BLS Polymers, SFC Environmental Technologies and Wiscon Industries on November 3.Antala Industries, whose Rs 23.33 crore SME IPO closes on November 2, is also expected to list on November 5.Four other SME companies are scheduled to close their public offerings on November 3 and list on November 6.These include Maxwell Engineering Solutions, which is raising Rs 57.64 crore; Johnsoncab Electricals, with an issue size of Rs 56.02 crore; Vectras Enprocon, which is seeking Rs 53.05 crore; and HGS (India), with a Rs 34.56 crore offering.MK Sons Fine Jewels, Ajwa Projects and Carver Roboweld are scheduled to list on November 4. That takes the total number of expected listings during the week to 13, including five mainboard companies, subject to the final exchange schedules.Disclosure: This article has been written by Podishetti Akash, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. primary.title: Cyclone 'Murasu' forms over Bay of Bengal
primary.description: Bhubaneswar: The deep depression over the Bay of Bengal on Sunday intensified into cyclonic storm 'Murasu', prompting the Odisha government to step up preparedness in the southern region of the state, officials said.In its latest bulletin, the IMD said cyclone 'Murasu' has formed over the Bay of Bengal and is likely to make landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 3.Cyclone 'Murasu' (war drum), named by India, is "set to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross the land in Andhra Pradesh coast with wind speeds of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narsapur by morning of November 3," it said.Odisha's Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the state government has already announced a high alert in the southern region.The government has also ordered the evacuation of people from low-lying areas and hilly terrain.Director of Meteorological Centre, Bhubaneswar, Manorama Mohanty, said Odisha will receive rainfall from November 2, and the intensity of rain will increase on November 3 and November 4 under the influence of the cyclone.

primary.title: Dalal Street Weak Ahead: Nifty stands on firmer footing, but can it break past 23,450?
primary.description: The Indian equity markets staged a strong recovery during the week, reversing part of their recent losses and ending on a positive note. The Nifty began the week on a relatively subdued footing but witnessed buying interest at lower levels, helping the Index recover and close above the psychologically important 23,000 mark. The trading range remained relatively wide, with the Nifty oscillating in a 730.75-point range. Volatility eased considerably; the India VIX declined by 9.25% to 15.30, reflecting some moderation in market uncertainty. The headline Index ended the week with a net gain of 453.10 points (+2.00%).135396555The most significant technical development during the week was the Nifty's ability to reclaim its 200-week Moving Average, presently placed at 22,700.18. This is an important positive development, especially after the index slipped below this long-term trend indicator. However, the broader technical structure remains vulnerable, and the recent recovery should not yet be interpreted as a confirmed trend reversal. The 200-week MA is now expected to serve as the principal reference point for the markets over the coming weeks.The Nifty's ability to defend this level on a sustained basis will be crucial in determining whether the present recovery develops into a more meaningful upward move. Conversely, a renewed breach of this average would weaken the recovery attempt and leave the Index exposed to further downside pressure.135398740The coming week is likely to see the markets attempting to consolidate their recent gains, with a cautiously positive undertone. The levels of 23,300 and 23,450 are likely to act as immediate resistance points. The supports are expected to come in at 22,750 and 22,525.The weekly RSI stands at 43.29; it stays neutral and does not show any divergence against the price. The weekly MACD remains bearish and trades below its signal line. A big white candle at the 200-week MA reinforces the credibility of this support point.135398772The pattern analysis of the weekly chart shows that the Nifty is presently attempting to stabilize near an important long-term support confluence. The 200-week MA coincides closely with a trendline support drawn from the major lows of early 2025, making the 22,700 zone technically significant. The immediate challenge for the Nifty will be to sustain above the reclaimed support while negotiating the overhead supply zones. The 20-week Bollinger Band midpoint, presently at 23,696.04, represents an additional resistance area.In the coming week, market participants should approach the markets with cautious optimism but avoid adopting an aggressively bullish stance. The recovery above the 200-week MA is encouraging, but the absence of stronger momentum confirmation warrants a measured approach. Fresh buying should remain selective. It would also be prudent to protect gains after sharp rebounds instead of chasing prices at higher levels. A stockspecific approach, disciplined risk management, and close monitoring of the Nifty's behavior around its 200-week MA should remain the central strategy for the coming week.In our look at Relative Rotation Graphs, we compared various sectors against the CNX500 (NIFTY 500 Index), representing over 95% of the free-float market cap of allthe listed stocks.The Relative Rotation Graph (RRG) shows a distinct change of leadership in the markets.The Nifty Sector Index has rolled inside the leading quadrant. The Nifty Bank, Media, Pharma, and IT Indices are inside the leading quadrant as well. These groups are likely to relatively outperform the benchmark.The Metal Index has sharply rolled back inside the weakening quadrant. The Realty, Midcap100, and the Auto sector Indices are also inside the weakening quadrant.Only Nifty FMCG and Energy Sector Indices are inside the lagging quadrant. However, both of these are seeing a sharp improvement in their relative momentum against the broader markets.The Nifty Infrastructure Index has rolled inside the improving quadrant. The PSE, PSU Bank, and the Financial Services Indices are also inside this quadrant. They may see an overall improvement in their momentum against the broader Nifty 500 Index.Important Note: RRG™chartsshow the relative strength and momentum of a group ofstocks. In the above Chart, they show relative performance against the NIFTY500 Index (Broader Markets) and should not be used directly as buy or sell signals.

articles.title: India's industrial output growth slows to 6.7% in September as manufacturing, consumer durables lose momentum
articles.description: India’s industrial output growth slowed to 6.7% in September from 7.8% in August, missing market expectations of 7.3%. Manufacturing and electricity growth moderated, while mining contracted 6.2%. Industrial production grew 6.8% in April-September, up from 4.4% a year earlier.
